claims.claim: Chevron reported second quarter 2026 earnings of $12.1 billion.
U.S. upstream production was a record in the quarter.
U.S. refinery crude throughput was a record in the quarter.
Total debt was cut by a record $8.4 billion in the quarter.
Reported earnings were $6.11 per diluted share in 2Q26.
2Q25 reported earnings were $2,490 million, or $1.45 per diluted share.
Return on capital employed was 21.4 percent in 2Q26.
Return on capital employed was 6.2 percent in 2Q25.
Adjusted earnings (non-GAAP) were $12.0 billion, or $6.06 per diluted share, in 2Q26.
2Q25 adjusted earnings were $3,053 million, or $1.77 per diluted share.
The quarter included an asset sale gain of $230 million.
The quarter included pension settlement costs of $86 million.
Foreign currency effects decreased earnings by $49 million in the quarter.
Sales and other operating revenues were $67,199 million in 2Q26 versus $44,375 million in 2Q25.
Depreciation, depletion and amortization was $6,082 million versus $4,344 million a year ago.
Cash flow from operations was $22.6 billion in 2Q26.
Cash flow from operations excluding working capital (non-GAAP) was $19.7 billion.
Free cash flow (non-GAAP) was $18.1 billion.
Adjusted free cash flow (non-GAAP) was $15.4 billion.
Capex was $4.5 billion in the quarter.
Affiliate capex was $0.3 billion in the quarter.
Results included $1.4 billion in favorable timing effects.
The release defines timing effects as mark-to-market of financial derivatives prior to physical delivery plus the impact of LIFO inventory accounting.
Upstream earnings were $8,182 million in 2Q26.
U.S. upstream earnings were $3,541 million and international upstream earnings were $4,641 million.
Worldwide net oil-equivalent production was 4,070 MBOED.
Production was 20 percent above 2Q25.
The production increase was attributed to legacy Hess assets and growth in the Permian Basin and Gulf of America.
U.S. liquids realization was $70.80 per barrel.
U.S. natural gas realization was $0.91/mcf versus $1.75 a year ago.
Average Brent spot price was $104/bbl versus $68 a year ago.
International production was reduced by curtailments in the Partitioned Zone due to the Middle East conflict.
Downstream earnings were $4,868 million, comprising $2,411 million U.S. and $2,457 million international.
Downstream earnings reflected higher refined product margins and higher Chevron Phillips Chemical earnings.
U.S. refinery crude unit inputs were a record 1,070 MBD.
U.S. crude unit capacity utilization was over 97 percent.
International refinery crude inputs fell 10 percent versus 2Q25.
International refined product sales fell 13 percent versus 2Q25.
The international downstream volume declines were due to Middle East supply disruptions and weaker gasoline and diesel demand.
U.S. refined product sales fell 4 percent on lower gasoline demand.
The release provides no earnings, production or capex guidance.
The release notes Chevron publishes a separate quarterly "Sensitivities and Forward Guidance" document on its website.
The structural cost reduction program targets $3-4 billion versus 2024 levels by the end of 2026, and is the only forward target stated in the release.
Chevron achieved $3 billion of annual run-rate structural cost reductions, six months early.
Hess-related synergies of $1.5 billion annual run-rate were achieved.
Total debt was $37,075 million at June 30, 2026 versus $40,758 million at December 31, 2025.
Net debt (non-GAAP) was $28,545 million at June 30, 2026.
Net debt-to-CFFO (non-GAAP) was 0.6x.
The quarter included $3,504 million of dividends paid.
The quarter included $3,117 million of share repurchases.
The Board declared a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share, payable September 10, 2026.
There was a $2,945 million working capital inflow in the quarter.
The release itself isolates both the $1.4 billion of timing effects and the $2,945 million working capital effect.
The lower U.S. natural gas realization ($0.91/mcf versus $1.75) was cited as an offset to U.S. upstream earnings.
DD&A of $6,082 million was cited as an offset to U.S. upstream earnings.
claims.note: Basis mismatch: $6,082 million is consolidated company-wide DD&A from the income statement. The release cites only "higher depreciation, depletion and amortization" as a U.S. upstream offset and discloses no segment DD&A amount.

claims.claim: Chevron completed the sale of the Hong Kong downstream fuels and lubricants businesses.
The Asia-Pacific downstream package (50 percent of Singapore Refining Company and related assets) is expected to close in 2027.
Chevron signed a 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft for approximately 2.67 gigawatts of behind-the-meter capacity for a West Texas data center.
The release discloses no capital cost or earnings contribution for the Microsoft power agreement.
